notes: §2002:7.2.5.2 GR1: standard arithmetic is used for every compile-time operation. At --std 2002 CompileTimeArithmetic.For selects Standard2002 (DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticIsStandardDecimal changes at 2014): the standard intermediate data item of §2002:8.8.1.3.1.1 holds 32 significant digits, an operand is converted into it (§2002:8.8.1.3.1 r1), each sum, product and quotient is the exact result truncated to 32 digits (§2002:8.8.1.3.2, §2002:8.8.1.3.4, §2002:8.8.1.3.5), a subtraction is the sum with the negated operand (§2002:8.8.1.3.3), and a value outside 10^-999 through 10^1000 - 10^968 is refused (§2002:8.8.1.3.1 r2). The witness prints 10^30 * 100 + 9 - 10^30 * 100 as 0 and 2 / 3 * 3 as 1, where the 34-digit engine of 2014 gives 9 and 2 (kb/Work PB5575). The run-time ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD engine still uses the 34-digit model; that arm stays open in PB5575.
